test_title: RRB NTPC - Graduate 2025 (CBT 2) Advanced Full Test - 05
subject: general
question: A group with 17 members had a mean score of 15, while another group with n members had a mean score of 12. If their combined mean was 13.7, then find the value of n.
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Apply the **Alligation** method to find the ratio of members in the two groups.

Difference 1 (Group 1 − Combined) = 15 − 13.7 = 1.3

Difference 2 (Combined − Group 2) = 13.7 − 12 = 1.7

Ratio of members (Group 1 : Group 2) = 1.7 : 1.3 = 17 : 13

Since the number of members in Group 1 is given as **17**, the value of **n** must be **13**.

**∴ The correct answer is 13.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Mean score** of Group 1 = 15, **Members** = 17; **Mean score** of Group 2 = 12, **Members** = n; **Combined mean** = 13.7

**Formula Used:** Combined Mean = (n₁ × x̄₁ + n₂ × x̄₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d99ea3c21ff09556bcd945146ba8607d1ffa91897f6e9adf8b58909636d4f2ba.png] 

⇒ 13.7 = (17 × 15 + n × 12) ÷ (17 + n)

⇒ 13.7 × (17 + n) = 255 + 12n

⇒ 232.9 + 13.7n = 255 + 12n

⇒ 13.7n − 12n = 255 − 232.9

⇒ 1.7n = 22.1

⇒ n = 22.1 ÷ 1.7

⇒ n = 13

**∴ The correct answer is 13.**

**__Additional Information__**

Arithmetic Mean

The **Mean** is the sum of all observations divided by the total number of observations. Total Sum = Mean × Total Count.

Weighted Average

When combining two groups with different sizes n₁ and n₂ and averages A₁ and A₂, the combined average is Aₐvg = (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Alligation Rule in Averages

The ratio of the number of items in two groups is the inverse ratio of the deviations of their averages from the combined average.</p
